title: Magic vs Wishup: Pricing and Help Compared
summary: Looking at Magic vs Wishup? Compare pricing, billing cycles, and coverage so you know what each plan costs.
body_markdown:
Magic and Wishup sell different hours and bill on different cycles. Magic lists 40-hour weekly plans billed every four weeks. Wishup lists monthly plans by assistant type. Whether you get after-hours help depends on the plan.


**TLDR:**


- Magic plans renew every four weeks. Wishup’s reported prices are monthly.
- Wishup’s Prime and Elite plans cost about 28% more per year: $23,988 for Prime vs $18,720 for Magic’s Virtual Assistant, and $35,988 for Elite vs $28,080 for Magic’s Executive Assistant.
- Wishup’s entry plan, Prime, lists at $1,999/month on its pricing page (checked November 2026). The page doesn’t list a part-time plan or hours per day.
- Magic’s $540/week Executive Assistant plan includes 40 dedicated hours plus 10 hours/week of Magic 24/7 work.


## Wishup offers remote assistants for recurring tasks


Wishup is a virtual assistant service for businesses that need remote assistants to handle recurring tasks, such as scheduling, data entry, and email management. Its pricing page lists Prime, Elite, and US-based VA plans, a dedicated VA manager, and free VA replacement. Based on publicly available information as of November 2026.


## Magic selects, trains, and coaches your assistant


Magic finds, trains, and coaches a[human virtual assistant](https://getmagic.com/virtual-assistant/) who takes responsibility for tasks such as following up with leads. Your assistant uses AI to get more done, while Magic handles onboarding and replacement handovers.


On your first call, Magic asks about your business and goals and which tasks you want to hand off. From there, Magic picks a candidate from the top 0.5% of applicants and matches them to your needs before they start in your tools. You don’t review resumes or run interviews.


Before your assistant starts, Magic trains them on your tools and the way you like work done. If you run outbound sales, that might mean learning your CRM and your follow-up scripts. If you manage client accounts, it might mean learning your invoicing system and payment terms. Once your assistant is live, they get weekly one-on-one coaching from Magic, so they keep improving without you spending time managing them.


Every Magic assistant also uses AI. Magic sets up and pays for a[Claude account](https://claude.com/product/overview) for each assistant, so you add no[Claude subscription](https://claude.com/pricing) . Assistants are[trained on Claude](https://getmagic.com/claude) before they start, including checking its work before anything reaches you. A Magic coach then helps your assistant automate parts of your work, such as lead follow-up and prospect research, so one person handles more.

Magic assistant pricing was checked November 18, 2026. Sales offers weekly billing at different rates; part-time plans are available.


Wishup also lists a US-based VA plan at $5,400/month.


Wishup’s prices of $1,999 (Prime), $2,999 (Elite), and $5,400 (US-based) come from its pricing page, checked November 2026. The page lists monthly prices only, with no hours per day and no part-time plan. Based on publicly available information as of November 2026.


Wishup’s pricing page lists a dedicated VA manager but doesn’t state weekly hours. Magic’s listed plans are 40 hours a week with a dedicated assistant.


For a weekly view of Magic’s cost, the Virtual Assistant plan is $360 a week for 40 hours, billed as $1,440 every four weeks. The Executive Assistant plan is $540 a week, billed as $2,160 every four weeks.


Plan for plan, Wishup costs more. Its Prime plan is $5,268 a year more than Magic’s Virtual Assistant plan, and its Elite plan is $7,908 a year more than Magic’s Executive Assistant plan. That’s about 28% more in both cases. Wishup’s pricing page also advertised 20% off annual plans in November 2026. The figures here are monthly list prices.


## Magic’s full-time Executive Assistant plan includes after-hours help


With Magic’s full-time[Executive Assistant plan](https://getmagic.com/executive-assistant/) , you get 10 hours a week of Magic 24/7 work at no extra cost, handled by a separate team of human assistants.


Your dedicated Magic assistant works 40 hours a week on your schedule.


Magic 24/7 is a separate group of human assistants available around the clock. Your dedicated assistant keeps their scheduled hours; the separate team handles requests outside those hours, within your weekly allowance, as part of[how Magic works](https://getmagic.com/how-it-works/) .


> Example: If you need urgent prospect research while your assistant is offline, you can message Magic 24/7 to handle it.


## Magic handles replacement handovers and allows cancellation anytime


[Magic](https://getmagic.com/about/) has no long-term contract, and you can cancel anytime.


If you aren’t satisfied for any reason during your first two weeks, Magic makes it right or gives you a full refund.


You meet your assistant before you commit. After your call, you decide whether to work together and choose a start date. You pay nothing until you start working with your assistant, and there are no hidden fees.


If you need a new assistant, Magic finds the replacement and handles the handover. Magic selects someone for your needs, trains them before they start, and onboards them into your tools. Wishup’s pricing page lists free VA replacement and VA knowledge transfer with a dedicated account manager (based on publicly available information as of November 2026).


Magic also handles HR and pay, and gives your assistant weekly one-on-one coaching. If you run sales calls or do paid client work, that’s time you get back.


## Choose Magic for a 40-hour weekly assistant with after-hours help included


Wishup is a good fit if you prefer its platform or want a US-based assistant, its highest and most expensive plan. Magic is a good fit if you want a better price, no long-term contract, weekly one-on-one coaching from Magic, and after-hours help included with a full-time Executive Assistant plan. Based on publicly available information as of November 2026. Our[Magic vs Prialto](https://getmagic.com/blog/magic-vs-prialto/) and[Magic vs Wing Assistant](https://getmagic.com/blog/magic-vs-wing/) comparisons describe other alternatives.


For example, your Magic assistant can contact every new lead and follow up, asking for your input if a decision needs it. That gives you more time for sales calls. Magic selects your assistant from the[top 0.5% of applicants](https://getmagic.com/how-it-works/) after a short call about your business. There’s nothing to prepare.[Book a free call](https://getmagic.com/getstarted/) .


**When should you choose Magic over Wishup for your business?**


Choose Magic if you want a dedicated assistant with company-run onboarding, weekly coaching, and replacement handovers. Magic’s full-time Executive Assistant plan also fits owners who need occasional after-hours help. Wishup may fit if you want to choose among Prime, Elite, or US-based assistant options.


**How do you compare Magic and Wishup pricing for your budget?**


Magic’s Executive Assistant plan costs $540 per week, billed at $2,160 every four weeks, or $28,080 for 52 weeks. Four-week billing produces 13 billing periods per year, so don’t compare that payment directly with Wishup’s reported monthly prices. Wishup’s prices come from a secondary source; confirm the current rate and included hours with Wishup before committing.


**Can you use Magic or Wishup for urgent work outside your assistant’s hours?**


Magic’s full-time Executive Assistant plan includes 10 hours of Magic 24/7 work each week, handled by a separate team while your dedicated assistant keeps their scheduled hours. For example, you can message that team for urgent prospect research while your assistant is offline. The available Wishup pricing sources don’t confirm after-hours coverage.


**How do you switch from Wishup to Magic without handling the replacement process yourself?**


Start with a short call about your business and goals; Magic selects your assistant, handles onboarding into your tools, and lets you choose a start date. Confirm your Wishup end date before setting that date, since a secondary source reports a month’s cancellation notice that hasn’t been confirmed on Wishup’s site. If you later need a different Magic assistant, Magic finds the replacement and handles the handover.


**What if you only need a few hours of assistant help each day?**


Magic offers part-time plans; ask about hours and pricing on a short call. Wishup’s reported Prime and Elite options include 4 hours per day, but those details come from South, another hiring provider, and aren’t confirmed by Wishup.


**Should you get Magic’s Virtual Assistant or Executive Assistant plan for lead follow-up?**


Magic’s Virtual Assistant plan covers recurring follow-ups, so lead follow-up alone doesn’t require an Executive Assistant plan. Choose Executive Assistant if you also want an experienced assistant handling executive priorities, meeting prep, travel, and follow-ups with the people involved.


**Do you need to buy AI subscriptions for your Magic assistant?**


No, Magic provides and pays for a Claude account for every assistant. Your assistant receives training before starting and checks AI-generated work before sending it to you.


**Can your assistant follow up with leads without waiting for you at every step?**


Yes, your Magic assistant can contact every new lead and keep following up until each prospect responds. Your assistant brings you in when a decision needs your input, leaving you more time for sales calls.


**In a Magic vs Wishup comparison, what if you need a US-based assistant?**


Wishup has reported US-based VA options, while Magic hires assistants in the Philippines and Latin America. If location is a firm requirement, confirm availability directly with Wishup because the US-based options in this comparison come from a secondary source.


**What if you want to start with one assistant and add a team later?**


You can start with one Magic assistant and move to Magic Teams for three or more assistants. Teams includes custom hiring, training, scheduling, and a success coach from day one, with discounts at scale.


**What happens if you’re unhappy with your Magic assistant during the first two weeks?**


If you aren’t satisfied for any reason during your first two weeks, Magic makes it right or gives you a full refund. Contact Magic during that period to discuss what needs to change.


**When do you start paying for your Magic assistant?**


You pay nothing until you start working with your assistant. Before that, you meet the assistant Magic selects, decide whether to work together, and choose a start date.


**How does Magic screen your assistant before you meet them?**


Magic screens resumes, gives candidates an online assessment with an English test, and conducts a live video interview. Candidates must then pass Magic’s live training; Magic selects assistants from the top 0.5% of applicants.


**How does weekly coaching work for your Magic assistant?**


Magic gives your assistant weekly one-on-one coaching and stays involved after they start. A Magic coach also helps your assistant automate parts of your work, such as invoice matching, so one person can handle more.
